focus: traceability closure plus adversarial correctness replay

findingDetails.title: Persistent hook disable flags remain invisible to the suppression check
findingDetails.claim: The setup check can report hooks active while the checkout persistent hook-flags file disables the master or preflight path.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Re-read the checker and its cited environment-only branch; no persistent-file read is present in that branch.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The check may intentionally report process environment only, while persistent flags are an independent runtime control.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: A test proving the checker intentionally excludes persisted flags and separately reports effective hook state would refute the mismatch.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The replayed checker branch reads process.env only; prior scope proof identifies the hook-flags parser and preflight consumer.

findingDetails.title: AI-hook registration accepts a marker in the wrong event or command shape
findingDetails.claim: A marker string in a hooks section is treated as registration without validating the runtime event or command target.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Re-read the predicate and positive fixture; both confirm substring matching and a SessionStart fixture rather than schema validation.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Some adapters may validly load the advisory from a non-tool event; the active runtime contract still requires event-specific validation.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Per-adapter tests proving every accepted event and command shape is valid and invokes the advisory would narrow or refute the claim.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The helper is shared by adapter checks, and the positive Codex fixture exercises the permissive predicate.

findingDetails.title: Relative PATH lookup can resolve a spawned executable from the inspected checkout
findingDetails.claim: A relative PATH entry can make child executable resolution depend on files in the repository being inspected.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Re-read the spawn call and checked whether it uses an absolute executable path; it passes the command value through PATH lookup. safeGitEnv() was not re-read in this iteration.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: safeGitEnv() may replace PATH with absolute trusted directories, which would close this path; that remains the key unresolved counterevidence.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Direct evidence that safeGitEnv() removes relative PATH entries and a fixture proving a repository-local executable is never selected would refute the case.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The path-resolution boundary is the common runCommand child-process wrapper.

findingDetails.title: Allowlist parsing follows a repository-controlled symlink while reading patterns
findingDetails.claim: An inspected repository can steer the checker to read a host file through a symlink used as an allowlist candidate.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Re-read candidate selection and the file read; no realpath containment or symlink rejection appears in the cited path.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Only text lines are consumed as patterns, so impact depends on whether those lines are surfaced in report details; the external-file read itself remains repository-steered.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: A realpath containment check or test proving symlink candidates are rejected before reading would refute the disclosure path.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The read occurs at the shared allowlist-pattern loader after candidate selection.
